title: ARMS AND GENTLE CORE
subtitle: SEATED FIRST, THEN WALL AND STANDING. NO FLOOR TODAY. KIND HIPS.

script.welcome: Good morning Pam. I'm Stratton. Friday is arms and gentle core, about eleven minutes. We stay seated for the first half, then a few wall and standing moves with the chair nearby. No floor today. Pain-free only, and a smaller range is perfectly fine on sore-joint days. Well done for showing up.
script.start: Whenever you're ready. Sit tall near the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat, easy breath.
script.nextExercise: Next one. Settle in. No rush.
script.lastSet: Last one of these. Keep it comfortable.
script.complete: That's us, Pam. Lovely work. A proper little break from the desk and another day in the book. Have a sip of water. See you tomorrow.
script.pause: Paused. Take all the time you need.
script.resume: Back with you. Easy as we go.

exercises.name: SEATED KNEE LIFTS
exercises.cue: Sit tall near the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat and hip-width, hands resting lightly on the sides of the seat. For about twenty seconds, march gently: lift one knee a few inches, lower with control, then the other. Easy rhythm to wake the middle. Keep the torso tall and quiet. If the front of the left hip complains, make the left lift smaller or just lift the heel. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness. A smaller lift is perfect.
exercises.speakStart: Seated knee lifts to warm the middle. Two easy rounds of twenty seconds. March gently, one knee then the other. Tall and steady. Smaller is fine.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Feet flat. Easy breath.
exercises.speakDone: Knee lifts done. Nicely warmed up.

exercises.name: SEATED ROW
exercises.cue: Stay seated tall, feet flat. Empty hands or very light hand weights. Reach the arms forward at chest height, then draw the elbows back close to your sides, squeezing the shoulder blades gently together. Ten calm reps. Keep the shoulders soft and down, neck long. Empty hands are always allowed. Stop if any joint feels sharp; smaller range is fine on sore days.
exercises.speakStart: Seated row. Two sets of ten. Reach forward, draw the elbows back, gentle squeeze between the shoulders. Empty hands are fine.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty five seconds. Arms down. Shoulders soft.

exercises.name: SEATED OVERHEAD PRESS
exercises.cue: Sit tall, feet flat, core lightly braced. Empty hands or very light weights at shoulder height, palms forward. Press up slowly toward the ceiling, only as high as feels comfortable for your shoulders, then lower with control. Eight calm reps. No arching the back. If the shoulders are sore today, press only to forehead height or do one arm at a time. Stop for any sharp pain.
exercises.speakStart: Seated overhead press. Two sets of eight. Press up gently, only as high as feels kind, then lower slowly. Empty hands are fine.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty five seconds. Hands in the lap. Easy breath.

exercises.name: SEATED FIGURE FOUR
exercises.cue: Still seated tall, feet flat. Cross the left ankle lightly over the right knee into a gentle figure-four. Do not push the left knee down. Optional tiny hinge forward from the hips for a mild stretch in the outer left hip. Breathe slowly for about twenty seconds. Second set may repeat left or try the other side if it feels kind. If the front of the left hip pinches, skip this one entirely. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness.
exercises.speakStart: Seated figure four for the outer hip. Two holds of about twenty seconds. Left ankle lightly over the right knee. Sit tall, no forcing. Skip it if the front of the hip pinches.
exercises.speakRest: Fifteen seconds. Uncross gently. Easy breath.

exercises.name: WALL PUSH UPS
exercises.cue: Stand facing a clear wall, feet about arm's length away, hands on the wall at about shoulder height and a little wider than shoulders. Soften the elbows and lean your chest gently toward the wall, then press back to straight arms. Eight calm reps. Keep the body in one quiet line from head to heels — no sagging hips. Closer feet make it easier; farther feet make it a touch harder. Empty hands only. Stop for any sharp shoulder or wrist pain.
exercises.speakStart: Up to the wall now. Wall push ups. Two sets of eight. Soft lean in, press away calmly. Closer feet if you want it easier.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty five seconds. Hands down. Easy breath.
exercises.speakDone: Wall push ups done. Strong and steady.

exercises.name: STANDING HIP FLEXOR
exercises.cue: Stand beside the chair with the right hand lightly on the chair back. Step the left foot back about half a step — not a deep lunge — both feet pointing forward, knees soft. Gently tuck the pelvis under (belt buckle toward the ribs) until you feel a mild stretch at the front of the left hip. A tiny lean is enough. Breathe slowly for about twenty-five seconds. Small and kind, never aggressive. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness.
exercises.speakStart: Standing hip flexor, left leg back. Two holds of about twenty five seconds. Small step back, pelvis tucked, tiny lean. Kind and small.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Feet together. Easy breath.

exercises.name: CHAIR BALANCE
exercises.cue: Stand behind or beside the sturdy chair with one or both hands on the chair back. Shift your weight onto one foot and lift the other heel, or the whole foot just an inch, for about fifteen seconds. Then switch sides. Eyes on a fixed point ahead, stand tall, breathe. Hold the chair as firmly as you need — that is the point of it. If the left hip grumbles when standing on it, keep the toes of the other foot lightly touching the floor. Stop if anything feels sharp or wobbly in a worrying way.
exercises.speakStart: Chair balance to finish. Two rounds of about fifteen seconds each side. Hands on the chair, lift one foot a little, eyes ahead. Hold on as much as you like.
exercises.speakRest: Fifteen seconds. Both feet down. Easy breath.
exercises.speakDone: Balance done. That's the session, Pam. Lovely work. See you tomorrow.
